## Code & API Design

- **No warnings in code you write:** Treat TypeScript, React, and `astro check` warnings and hints (including `@deprecated` notices) as errors. Any file you add or touch must be clean. Run `npx astro check` and confirm the files you changed report no new issues before considering the work done. Do not silence a warning with an ignore directive when a correct fix exists. Example: a form `onSubmit` handler that only calls `preventDefault()` should type its argument as `React.SyntheticEvent`, not the deprecated `React.FormEvent`. (Note: the repo has pre-existing warnings/errors in unrelated files; this rule is about not *introducing* new ones, not fixing the backlog.)
- **No booleans in caller-facing APIs:** When designing options for schemas, frontmatter fields, function signatures, or component props, prefer string enums (e.g. `randomize: 'none' | 'within-sections'`) over booleans (e.g. `randomize: true`). Booleans are unreadable at the call site -- the reader has to remember what `true` means -- and they paint you into a corner if a third state is ever needed. Only reach for a boolean when there is genuinely no third option, and even then prefer a named-variant string when reasonable.

## Critical Rules

### Links
- Internal: `/blog/slug/`, `/glossary/term/`
- External: use plain `https://` URLs (the `remarkExternalLinks` plugin auto-adds `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`)
- Amazon affiliate: `&tag=notesfromatoo-20`
- **Glossary auto-linking (blog posts only):** Glossary terms in blog post content are automatically linked at build time via `linkGlossaryTerms()` in `src/utils/glossaryLookup.ts`. Each term is linked a maximum of 2 times per post. Common terms are excluded: scrum, agile, sprint, feedback, slack. Links are not added inside headings, images, figures, or existing links. Do not manually add links to glossary terms in blog posts. Glossary entries themselves are not auto-linked; they may include 4--5 manual internal links to relevant blog posts where appropriate.
- **Glossary external links live in the reference section, not the body.** In almost all cases a glossary entry's body prose should contain no external (`https://`) links. Name the source in the text (e.g. "Rebecca Wirfs-Brock argues...") and put the actual link in the `resourceLinks` HighlightBox (or `relatedBooks`) at the bottom. Internal links (`/blog/...`, `/glossary/...`) may still appear inline. Only inline an external link in the body when the prose would be incomprehensible without it, which is rare.

### Images
- Store in `images/` subdirectory within content folder
- Import at top of MDX file: `import Img from '@/content/blog/slug/images/img.jpg'`
- Use `<Figure src={Img} alt="description" caption="caption" />`
- Always provide meaningful alt text

### Content Guidelines
- **Excerpts/descriptions:** Must be human-authored, never AI-generated
- **Related terms:** Must reference valid glossary slugs; update bidirectionally
- **Dates:** Always YYYY-MM-DD format
- **Directory structure:** Always `{slug}/index.mdx` pattern
- **Curly quotes:** In all user-facing text (blog posts, glossary entries, pages), use curly (typographer's) quotes and apostrophes (' ' " ") instead of straight quotes (' "). Straight quotes are a typewriter-era holdover; curly quotes are the correct typographic form. See [Practical Typography](https://practicaltypography.com/straight-and-curly-quotes.html). Note: YAML frontmatter values and code samples should keep straight quotes as they are not displayed typographically.
- **No em dashes:** The author does not use em dashes (—) in writing. Use a colon, comma, or restructure the sentence instead.
- **No non-breaking spaces:** Never use Unicode non-breaking spaces (U+00A0) or other invisible Unicode whitespace characters. Use only regular ASCII spaces (U+0020). Non-breaking spaces cause subtle rendering and parsing issues and are difficult to spot in source files.
- **Updated date on refreshed posts:** When a pre-existing blog post or glossary entry receives a substantive content update (not mechanical changes like category tags, footnote migrations, link fixes, or quote conversions), set the `lastUpdated` frontmatter field to the current date. This is displayed on the page and included in JSON-LD as `dateModified`.
- **Anti-pattern glossary titles:** Individual anti-pattern glossary entries use the convention `'Name - Anti-Pattern'` in the title (e.g., `'Scrummerfall - Anti-Pattern'`, `'Fake Agile - Anti-Pattern'`). Collection entries that list many anti-patterns use the plural form without the dash (e.g., `'Agile Anti-Patterns'`, `'ScrumMaster Anti-Patterns'`).

### Redirects
- Configured in `src/constants/redirects.ts` (a typed `Record<string, string>` imported by `astro.config.mjs`); Astro compiles these to Netlify `_redirects` format (301s) during build
- **Trailing slashes:** Only add the trailing-slash version of a redirect (e.g., `'/old-path/'`). Do NOT add both `'/old-path/'` and `'/old-path'` for the same route. Astro handles both variants automatically, and duplicating them causes route collision warnings that will become hard errors in future Astro versions.
- Old category slugs have been mapped to current categories (e.g., `leadership` -> `modern-leadership-and-organizational-change`)
- Expired virtual course URLs redirect to the corresponding course type page (e.g., CSM, CSPO, CSD, A-CSM)
- When adding new redirects, place them in the appropriate commented section (courses, categories, blog posts, glossary, etc.)
- Glossary `aliases` field is for search only -- it does not create URL routes. Use a redirect in `src/constants/redirects.ts` if an old glossary URL needs to resolve.
- **No redirects for `noIndex` pages or short-lived pages.** Redirects exist to preserve inbound links and accumulated search equity. A `noIndex` page was never in the search index, and a page that only lived for a week (or days) has not accumulated external links or rankings worth preserving. Skip the redirect when retiring or renaming either kind.

### Content Processing Plugins
The Astro config (`astro.config.mjs`) applies custom remark/rehype plugins during build:
- `remarkExternalLinks` - Auto-detects external links (`https://`/`http://`) and adds `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`
- `remarkGfm` - GitHub-flavored markdown (tables, strikethrough, etc.)
- `rehypeFootnoteLinks` - Processes markdown footnote syntax

Additionally, `linkGlossaryTerms()` (`src/utils/glossaryLookup.ts`) runs client-side on blog post pages to auto-link glossary terms (see Links section above).

### Common Mistakes to Avoid
- Using internal-style paths for external URLs (always use full `https://` URLs for external links)
- Referencing non-existent related terms or categories
- Missing alt text on images
- Forgetting to import components before using them
- AI-generating excerpts or meta descriptions
- Using deprecated `<Footnotes>` component (use plain markdown footnotes)
- Adding both trailing-slash and non-trailing-slash versions of the same redirect (causes route collisions)
- Adding redirects from a page's own path to itself with a trailing slash (e.g., `'/glossary': '/glossary/'`). Netlify already handles trailing slash normalization, so this creates an infinite redirect loop

## CTA / Popup System

Centralized in `src/constants/cta.ts` with two rendering components:
- `src/components/global/modal-popup.astro` — Popup on blog and glossary pages (30s delay, 15-day frequency cap)
- `src/components/global/cta-banner.astro` — Inline banner on homepage, blog index, and glossary index

**How it works:**
- `CTA_PRIMARY: CTAContent` — The active CTA copy (heading, body, button text, link)
- `CTA_VARIANT: CTAContent | null` — Set to `null` when no A/B test is running; populate with a `CTAContent` object to activate a second variant
- `AB_TEST_ENABLED` — Master switch; when `false`, always shows primary
- Both components conditionally render the variant block only when `CTA_VARIANT` is not null
- PostHog tracks button clicks via `data-ph-capture-attribute-*` attributes
- Modal frequency controlled via localStorage (`src/utils/storage.ts`)

**To update CTA copy:** Edit `CTA_PRIMARY` in `src/constants/cta.ts`. No component changes needed.
**CTA forms vs link buttons:** All popup/banner CTAs render a link button. The shared `FormSubmission` component (used by the newsletter section of pages, the modal popup, and the CTA banner) POSTs (Turnstile-gated) to `/api/newsletter-signup`, which forwards to Cakemail's Newsletter Subscribers form server-side. Its `source` prop applies a per-placement signup tag; see "General newsletter signup" above.
**To run an A/B test:** Populate `CTA_VARIANT` with a `CTAContent` object and set `AB_TEST_ENABLED = true`.

## Social Media Posting

Two skills cover social posting. Both defer to `.claude/skills/_social-posting-conventions.md`, the single source of truth for character limits, threading, hashtags, URL handling, and style, so the rules live in one place:

- **`/social-media-adapt`** - adapt one LinkedIn post into Mastodon + Bluesky threaded JSON in `social-media/temp/`.
- **`/evergreen-posting`** - generate a batch of evergreen reshares from the curated queue in `social-media/planning/`.

The Buffer scheduling pipeline lives in the separate `social-media-posting` repo (`npm run post`, `npm run batch`, `npm run validate`); see that repo's `CLAUDE.md` for pipeline behaviour (UTM, cover images, link-in-body, history). **Posting cadence and slot times are defined in code** (`social-media-posting/buffer-post/slotPlan.mjs`) and printed in the calendar file's header by `npm run calendar-audit -- --write`. Read it there; don't restate it, because a stale copy of that number has caused real over-scheduling.

**Content queue:** `social-media/planning/complete-social-media-calendar.md` is a curated, hand-maintained reshare queue; run `npm run calendar-audit` (in the posting repo) to flag drift against the live blog/glossary content.

## Analytics Data

### Post Engagement (`analytics/history.json`)

Permanent record of all social media posts with per-platform engagement metrics. Each post has: `id`, `created`, `posted`, `linkedin`, `mastodon`, `bluesky` (content text), `topics`, `links`, and `engagement` containing:
- **LinkedIn**: `reactions`, `comments`, `impressions`, `reach`, `engagementRate`
- **Mastodon**: `favorites`, `replies`, `reblogs`
- **Bluesky**: `likes`, `comments`, `reposts`

### PostHog Website Analytics (`analytics/posthog/`)

CSV exports from PostHog (updated via `npm run posthog-export`).
- **Pageviews by week, UTM source, and pathname** -- unique visitors per page per traffic source per week. UTM sources: `mastodon`, `linkedin`, `website`, `blog`, `chatgpt.com`, `None` (direct/organic). Older exports also contain `drip` (the retired email provider, now Cakemail); it is historical only -- current email traffic is not tagged `drip`.
- **Average session duration by UTM source by week** -- total sessions and average session length by referral channel.
- **Bounce rate by UTM source and pathname** -- bounced vs. total sessions and bounce rate percentage.
- **Entry path by UTM source** -- landing page performance by traffic source and campaign.
- **CTA button clicks by URL and referrer** -- clicks on CTA buttons broken down by page and referring source.

### Ahrefs SEO Data (`analytics/Ahrefs/`)

Periodic CSV exports. **Note: Ahrefs subscription has ended, so this data will not be updated.**
- **Organic keywords** -- keyword rankings, search volume, difficulty, position changes, traffic estimates, SERP features, intent classification.
- **Top pages** -- pages ranked by organic traffic, ranking keywords, referring domains, URL rating.
- **Backlinks** -- inbound links with domain rating, anchor text, follow/nofollow status, first/last seen dates.

### Google Analytics and Search Console (`analytics/google/`)

CSV exports covering user acquisition sources, page performance, search queries, devices, and countries.

### Connecting Posts to Website Traffic

The link between social engagement and website traffic is the URL:
1. A post in `history.json` has a `links` array (e.g. `["https://agilepainrelief.com/blog/some-post/"]`)
2. Buffer adds UTM parameters when posting (e.g. `?utm_source=mastodon`)
3. PostHog records the visit with the pathname and UTM source
4. Match on pathname to connect social post to website traffic

The `analytics/posthog/` CSVs and `analytics/history.json` together let you correlate social engagement with website traffic. Match the `links` array in `history.json` to PostHog pathnames, filtering by `utm_source` to isolate the referring channel.

## Environment Variables

The Astro **site** uses **no Cakemail credentials**. Browser signups (general newsletter, AI forms, quiz) POST to the `/api/newsletter-signup` Netlify function, which verifies a Cloudflare Turnstile token and forwards to a Cakemail hosted form — anonymous, so still no OAuth/HMAC. The one required server secret is **`TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY`** (Netlify env, read via `process.env`); the public Turnstile site key is a constant in `src/constants/turnstile.ts`. The post-course prefilled link stays fully client-side (Cakemail embed + DOI). See "Signup bot protection" and the quiz engine sections above. (The `email-automation/` CLI does use Cakemail credentials, read from the root `.env`; see `email-automation/CLAUDE.md`.)

**If you add a server endpoint that reads secrets, use `process.env.X`, not `import.meta.env.X`.** Astro/Vite inlines `import.meta.env` values into the SSR function bundle at build time, so env var updates only take effect after a redeploy. Reading from `process.env` resolves at runtime, so an updated Netlify env var is picked up on the next cold start with no redeploy required.

The PostHog CSV exporter (`scripts/posthog-export.ts`, run via `npm run posthog-export`) reads the root `.env` at runtime for:
- `POSTHOG_TOKEN` - PostHog personal API key with `insight:read` scope (EU endpoint, project 59984). The exporter writes `analytics/posthog/*.csv`.

The social media posting workflow (in the separate social media repo) requires:
- `BUFFER_API_TOKEN` - API token for Buffer's GraphQL API (create at Buffer developer settings)

## Development Workflow

```bash
npm run dev           # Development with drafts visible
npm run build         # Production build
npm run preview       # Preview production build
npm run links         # Lychee link-check across MDX content
npm run links:report  # Same, but write a markdown report to broken-links.md
npm run posthog-export # Update PostHog analytics CSVs in analytics/posthog/ (exporter: scripts/posthog-export.ts; needs POSTHOG_TOKEN in root .env, insight:read scope, EU endpoint, project 59984)
```

**Social media commands** (require the separate `social-media-posting` repo to be cloned alongside this repo):
```bash
npm run validate            # Pre-flight social-media/temp/ before posting (no token, no network)
npm run post                # Schedule the single post in social-media/temp/ via API
npm run post -- --now       # Publish immediately instead of queueing
npm run post -- --dry-run   # Preview API payloads without posting
npm run validate -- --file analytics/social-media-content-evergreen/<name>.json
npm run batch -- --file analytics/social-media-content-evergreen/<name>.json [--dry-run]
                            # Schedule an evergreen batch; marks the calendar + quiz seeds on success
npm run calendar-audit      # Queue vs live blog/glossary; --write refreshes the header counts
npm run reshare-report      # Rank posted queue items by clicks-per-reshare
npm run scrape              # Sync LinkedIn, Mastodon, and Bluesky metrics from Buffer to history.json
```

All of these resolve paths from cwd, so run them from this repo's root.

70	
71	`src/automation-sync.ts` exports `syncAutomation(config)`. It handles
72	markdown-to-HTML rendering, image-path rewriting, MJML wrapper injection
73	(via `src/render-email.ts`, shared with the newsletter CLI), merge-tag
74	substitution, and `upsertTemplate` calls. Each per-automation script (e.g.
75	`src/sync-postcourse-csm.ts`, `src/sync-welcome-newsletter.ts`) is a thin

79	(`EMAIL_FROM_NAME` / `EMAIL_FROM_EMAIL`), shared by the API client and the

84	It also inlines brand styles onto `<h1>`–`<h4>` (`styleHeadings`, called from

86	blue, both bold. Heading styles are inlined rather than left to the wrapper's

88	styles, which otherwise leaves headings rendering as plain bold-and-bigger.

98	   import { syncAutomation } from "./automation-sync";
99	
100	   syncAutomation({
101	     name: "<name>",
102	     emailsDir: resolve(__dirname, "../automations/<name>"),
103	     wrapperPath: resolve(__dirname, "../templates/course/post-wrapper.html"),
104	     imageBaseUrl: "https://agilepainrelief.com/images/email/<name>",

108	     // extraTestMergeTags?: (testEmail) => ({ foo: "bar" }),

115	### Idempotency
116	
117	Re-running a sync updates the existing Cakemail template by name rather than
118	creating a duplicate — `CakemailClient.upsertTemplate` looks up by exact
119	template name and PATCHes if found. Rename the template (in config) only if
120	you intend to orphan the old one.
121	
122	**Automation step caveat.** Updating a template does **not** propagate to
123	running Cakemail automations. Each automation step snapshots the template
124	content at the moment it was configured (empirically confirmed 2026-04-23).
125	After a content change, re-import the template in each affected automation
126	step via the Cakemail UI — unselect / reselect "Use a template", or swap to
127	a different template and back — to force a fresh pull.

158	## Newsletter sender (markdown-driven campaign)
159	
160	`src/send-newsletter.ts` renders a newsletter markdown file into HTML,
161	wraps it in the same MJML shell
162	used by the automation templates, and creates a draft campaign on the
163	`Newsletter Subscribers` list via the Cakemail `POST /campaigns` API.
164	
165	**The authoring + send workflow lives in the `/newsletter` skill**
166	(`.claude/skills/newsletter/SKILL.md`): markdown file format, frontmatter,
167	Obsidian callouts (`[!quote]` / `[!action]`), the required `courses.json`
168	block, the `--test-send` / `--send` flag flow, and the sender/compliance notes.
169	Use that skill to draft or send a newsletter. The command reference below is
170	retained for quick lookup.
171	
172	```bash
173	npm run send-newsletter -- --content newsletters/<file>.md [--test-send <email>] [--send | --schedule <day>] [--allow-past-courses] [--keep-on-error]
174	```
175	
176	Every run creates a **brand-new** campaign (`POST /campaigns`); there is no
177	idempotency. Re-running the command is therefore how the whole list gets
178	emailed twice. Before creating, the CLI queries `findCampaignsByName` and
179	**aborts** if a campaign of the same name (`{date} - {subject}`) already exists
180	in a committed state (scheduled / delivering / delivered). There is **no
181	`--force`**: delete the existing campaign in Cakemail, then re-run. Same-name
182	*drafts* don't block (they can't send); they're listed as a cleanup nudge.
183	
184	Flags:
185	- `--test-send <email>` creates the draft, then sends a `POST
186	  /campaigns/{id}/send-test` copy (`type=merged`) to the given address. This is
187	  the way to preview a newsletter: review it in your inbox and the Cakemail UI.
188	  **Preview-only: cannot be combined with `--send` or `--schedule`** (dispatch
189	  in a separate run). Combining preview with dispatch is what previously caused
190	  a "thought it was just a test" double-send.
191	- `--send` schedules the draft for immediate delivery (`POST
192	  /campaigns/{id}/schedule` with no date). Prompts `yes/no` before firing.
193	- `--schedule <day>` schedules delivery for the next `Mon|Tue|Wed|Thu|Fri` at
194	  10:00 AM Eastern (`POST /campaigns/{id}/schedule` with a `date` UNIX
195	  timestamp). Resolves to the soonest future 10am ET on that weekday; the
196	  `America/New_York` zone keeps it correct across EST/EDT. No confirmation
197	  prompt (the flag is the intent). Mutually exclusive with `--send`.
198	- `--allow-past-courses` bypasses the stale-course date check (the CLI aborts
199	  if `newsletters/courses.json` is missing/empty or holds a past-dated course).
200	- `--keep-on-error` leaves the draft in Cakemail if test-send or schedule
201	  fails. Default `DELETE /campaigns/{id}` keeps the UI tidy, since a failed
202	  send usually means re-running after a content fix.
203	
204	The campaign is sent from sender ID `SENDER_ID_MARK` (=
205	`mark@agilepainrelief.com`), not the `contact@` sender used for transactional
206	course emails. The payload sets `content.default_unsubscribe_link: true`, so
207	Cakemail appends its own unsubscribe link and mandated postal-address footer.
208	
209	**Greeting is code-owned, not authored.** `send-newsletter.ts` prepends the
210	greeting (`GREETING` = `Hi [firstname],`) to the body itself; the markdown file
211	must not contain one. `[firstname]` is Cakemail's no-fallback merge tag (blank
212	when the contact has no first name). NEVER use an empty fallback `[firstname,]`
213	— it's malformed and Cakemail prints the tag literally (this mailed the whole
214	list a literal `Hi [firstname,],` on 2026-06-26). A no-word fallback is
215	deliberate (Mark prefers a bare greeting to a generic word like "there"). If an
216	author still hand-writes a leading line containing `firstname`, `withGreeting()`
217	strips it and substitutes the canonical greeting, so a mistyped tag can't ship.

219	## Cakemail Data Model
220	
221	### Lists
222	| List | Purpose |
223	|------|---------|
224	| **Course Students** | All students. Custom attributes track dedup. Not used for sending. |
225	| **PostCourse CSM** | Adding a contact triggers 10-email CSM follow-up automation. Per-contact `firstname` and `newslettersignupurl` custom attributes drive template merge tags. |
226	| **Newsletter Subscribers** | Marketing newsletter campaigns and the `aiquiz` nurture sequence. |
227	
228	### Tags (broad categories, keep under 15)
229	- `CSM Student`, `CSPO Student` — course attendance
230	- Signup tags (`aiquiz`, the two-axis type/source tags) are applied browser-side by the Astro hosted-form POSTs, not by this CLI. See the root `CLAUDE.md` signup sections.
231	
232	### Refresher offers (free-seat promos to alumni)
233	
234	When a workshop has spare seats, we offer a free refresher to past students who opted in. The audience is built from tags, not a standing list. **Audience rule (apply all three filters):**
235	
236	1. **Include** anyone tagged `Interested - Refresher - {COURSE}` (e.g. `Interested - Refresher - CSM`).
237	2. **Exclude** anyone tagged `DO NOT NOTIFY - Refresher - {COURSE}` — a hard suppression. If a contact carries *both* the Interested and DO-NOT-NOTIFY tags, DO-NOT-NOTIFY wins.
238	3. **Exclude anyone who has already attended a refresher.** A refresher attendee carries a `Course - <date> - …` tag for the refresher *session* date, distinct from their original paid training. Cross-reference against the known refresher session dates below and drop matches. Don't offer the same person a second free refresher.
239	
240	**Known past refresher session dates** (extend this when you run a new one):
241	- `2026-03-05` — CSM refresher (Mar 5–6, 2026)
242	- `2025-07-14`, `2025-07-15` — CSPO refresher (Jul 14–15, 2025)
243	
244	**Maintenance note:** the date-list approach works but is brittle. The cleaner durable signal is a dedicated `Attended - Refresher - {COURSE}` tag applied to attendees of each free refresher — then filter 3 becomes a single tag check with no date table to maintain. Prefer adding that tag going forward, and reduce the date list as attendees get the tag.
245	
246	**Delivery:** use the dedicated `npm run send-refresher -- --content <promo>.md --audience <list>.csv` script (`src/send-refresher.ts`). It sends as a **direct (transactional) send** via `sendTransactional()` (`/v2/emails`), one rendered email per recipient, and does **not** create a standing Cakemail list. The transactional endpoint's `list_id` is only relay context (`Course Students`); it does not subscribe recipients as marketing contacts, so there's no list to maintain and no consent side effect. The script already sends from `SENDER_ID_MARK` (not the `SENDER_ID_CONTACT`/contact@ used by default transactional sends, since refresher promos go from Mark) and applies **no tags** — attendance tags (`Attended - Refresher - {COURSE}`) are added after the workshop, not when the offer goes out. Preview with `--test-send <email>` (sends one copy and stops); dispatch to the whole audience with `--send`. Unsubscribe is handled automatically: Cakemail appends an unsubscribe button to the transactional email's footer (confirmed by inspecting a test send), so no manual compliance footer is needed; the template's reply-to-opt-out p.s. is a friendly extra, not the sole mechanism.
247	
248	Source-of-truth audience today lives in the migration exports (`migration/all-people.csv`, `migration/subscribers-people.csv`); the filtered CSM list is materialized to `migration/refresher-csm-interested.csv`.
249	
250	### Custom Attributes (on "Course Students" list)
251	Pattern: `{type}_course_date`, `{type}_7day_prep_sent`, `{type}_2day_prep_sent`, `{type}_post_sent`
252	
253	Example for CSM: `csm_course_date`, `csm_7day_prep_sent`, `csm_2day_prep_sent`, `csm_post_sent`
254	
255	The `send-course-email` script sets these after successful sends and checks `*_sent`
256	attributes for dedup on subsequent runs.
257	
258	### Custom Attributes (on "PostCourse CSM" list)
259	Set at enrollment time by `send-course-email --email post --course CSM`:
260	- `firstname` — the student's first name from the Corsizio CSV. Referenced in templates
261	  as `[firstname,there]`, so students without a value see "Hello there!".
262	- `newslettersignupurl` — per-student prefilled Cakemail form link (to the Astro
263	  site's `/newsletter-subscribe/` page) that subscribes them to the Newsletter
264	  Subscribers list. Built by `buildPrefillSignupUrl()` in `src/signup-url.ts`.
265	  Referenced in templates as `[newslettersignupurl]`.
266	
267	Re-running `send-course-email` for a student who already exists on this list PATCHes
268	the existing contact's attributes rather than re-inserting (so re-enrollment refreshes
269	the signed URL).
270	
271	### Newsletter Opt-In (prefilled form link)
272	Post-course emails include a "Subscribe to the Newsletter" link pointing at the Astro
273	site's `/newsletter-subscribe/` page, with the student's email and first name prefilled
274	in the query string (and `auto_submit=1`). That page embeds a Cakemail form on the
275	Newsletter Subscribers list with double opt-in; Cakemail's form-prefill script fills and
276	submits it from the URL params, then sends the confirmation email.
277	
278	The placeholder `CAKEMAIL_NEWSLETTER_SIGNUP_URL` in post-course markdown templates is
279	replaced per-student inside `renderMarkdownEmail()` using `buildPrefillSignupUrl()` from
280	`src/signup-url.ts`. No HMAC signature, no server endpoint, no OAuth token — double
281	opt-in is the abuse guard (a forged link only mails a confirmation to the address that
282	owns it).
283	
284	## Environment
285	All env vars live in the **root-level `.env`** (one directory above this one), shared
286	with the Astro site. The CLI loads it via `src/load-env.ts` on import. Required keys:
287	
288	- `CAKEMAIL_REFRESH_TOKEN` — OAuth refresh token for this CLI. **Routine refresh is
289	  automatic:** every run exchanges it for a short-lived access token, and if Cakemail
290	  issues a rotated refresh token in that response, `cakemail-client.ts` writes the new
291	  value back to the root `.env` itself (no manual step). Only when the refresh token has
292	  fully **expired** (the client throws `Cakemail refresh token expired. Run: npm run
293	  refresh-cakemail`) do you run `npm run refresh-cakemail` to mint a new one from
294	  username + password and paste it into the root `.env`.
295	- `NEWSLETTER_SIGNUP_BASE_URL` — optional, defaults to `https://agilepainrelief.com`.
296	  Base URL for the per-student post-course newsletter subscribe link (the
297	  `/newsletter-subscribe/` page); override for local testing.
298	
299	List IDs and sender IDs live in `../shared/cakemail-constants.ts`, imported by
300	`src/cakemail-client.ts`.
301	
302	## Course Config
303	Create `courses/<type>-<location>.json` (e.g. `csm-virtual.json`, `cspo-virtual.json`, `csd-virtual.json`) with fields:
304	type, date, numberOfDays, muralLink, meetingInvite (object)
305	
306	`--course CSM` auto-detects the config by matching files in `courses/` whose name starts with the course type (case-insensitive); it errors if zero or multiple match.
307	
308	`meetingInvite` is a structured object, both fields copied off the same Zoom screen:
309	- `zoomUrl` — full Zoom one-click join URL (e.g. `https://us02web.zoom.us/j/...?pwd=...`). Drives the "JOIN the COURSE ZOOM MEETING" button. The `pwd=` token is Zoom's one-click join token.
310	- `invitationUrl` — Zoom's `/meetings/{id}/invitations?signature=...` link. The email links to it for "all other ways of joining" (phone dial-in numbers, dial-in passcode, SIP). We do **not** scrape or restate those details: Zoom maintains that page, so it stays current automatically when a dial-in number changes. The `signature` token is scoped to the meeting and lives for its lifetime.
311	
312	The former `passcode` field (plus a hardcoded dial-in number list) is gone. `send-course-email` rejects any config that still has `meetingInvite.passcode`, so an un-migrated config breaks loudly instead of sending a broken invite.
313	
314	Optional fields (have defaults):
315	- `duration` — daily start-end time, e.g. `"08:59-17:01"` (default). Drives both the calendar links and the displayed `{{var:class_times}}` in the pre-course emails (e.g. CSD uses `"12:30-17:00"` → "12:30 p.m. to 5:00 p.m.").
316	- `timezone` — IANA timezone, e.g. `"America/Toronto"` (default)
317	- `location` — e.g. `"Virtual"` (default), `"In-Person"`
318	- `googleDocsFolder` — only needed for CSM courses
319	- `dropboxFolder` — the **per-cohort mural export** Dropbox folder (post-course only). Shown in the post email as `{{var:training_folder}}`. This is where Mark exports the class's murals after the cohort; it is per-cohort and unrelated to the workbook.
320	- `workbookUrl` — optional per-cohort override for the hosted workbook link. Normally omitted (the link is resolved by course type; see below). Set it only for a one-off cohort that needs a different URL.
321	
322	### Post-course workbook link
323	
324	Two different links live in the post-course email, and they are deliberately separate:
325	
326	- **Mural export** — `{{var:training_folder}}`, from the per-cohort `config.dropboxFolder`. Changes every cohort. Still on Dropbox (out of scope for the workbook move).
327	- **Course workbook** — `{{var:workbook_link}}`, the workbook PDF hosted on the APR site. Resolved by `deriveWorkbookUrl(config)` in `src/course-config.ts`: (1) `config.workbookUrl` cohort override, else (2) `courses/workbook-urls.json[type]`, else `null` (course not yet migrated — its template then still hardcodes its own link).
328	
329	`courses/workbook-urls.json` maps course type → the current direct PDF URL on the APR site (`https://agilepainrelief.com/materials/<course>-<year>-q<quarter>-<hex>/<file>.pdf`). It is the **single place to update once per quarter** when the site's `/materials/` slug rotates. Must be the direct PDF URL (bare files have no folder index) with spaces `%20`-encoded.
330	
331	`{{var:workbook_link}}` appears in all three CSPO templates — `pre-7day` and `pre-2day` (the "Download the Digital Workbook" link, the pre-class firewall-critical one) and `post` — so migrating a course means switching each of its templates to the variable. (CSM/CSD still hardcode their Dropbox links pending migration.)
332	
333	When any email's template (pre or post) references `{{var:workbook_link}}`, that send (including `--dry-run`) requires a configured URL and runs `assertWorkbookReachable()`: a `HEAD` (falling back to a ranged `GET`) that **aborts on a non-200**, so a typo'd slug, an unpushed folder, or a filename mismatch can't email students a dead link. The check is scoped to `agilepainrelief.com/materials/` URLs. It proves the link is *live*, not that it's the *current* workbook. Templates that still hardcode a Dropbox link are unaffected until migrated.
334	
335	Derived automatically:
336	- `dateFormatted` (e.g. "Feb 17-18"), `daysOfWeek` (e.g. "Tuesday-Wednesday") — from `date` + `numberOfDays`
337	- `zoomLink` — from `meetingInvite.zoomUrl`
338	- The `{{var:meeting_invite}}` block — a short "Other ways to join" line linking to `meetingInvite.invitationUrl`
339	
340	Google Calendar and Outlook Calendar links are generated from config fields by `src/course-config.ts`.
341	
342	### Pre-course Email Template Placeholders
343	The pre-course HTML templates (`templates/course/pre-*.html`) use `{{var:name}}` variables
344	that are substituted locally in Node before sending raw HTML to Cakemail:
345	- `{{var:first_name}}`, `{{var:course_dates}}`, `{{var:class_times}}`, `{{var:meeting_invite}}`
346	- `{{var:google_calendar_url}}`, `{{var:outlook_calendar_url}}`
347	- `{{var:mural_link}}`, `{{var:zoom_link}}`, `{{var:google_docs_folder}}`
348	- `{{var:workbook_link}}` — the hosted course workbook PDF (see "Post-course workbook link"; despite the heading, the same variable is used by the pre-7day / pre-2day templates for the "Download the Digital Workbook" link)
349	
350	### Post-course Markdown Email Templates
351	Post-course emails are written in Markdown (`templates/course/post-csm.md`, `post-cspo.md`)
352	with YAML frontmatter for the subject line. At send time, Markdown is converted to HTML
353	via `marked` and injected into `templates/course/post-wrapper.html` (the MJML-compiled
354	header/footer shell).
355	
356	**Available variables in Markdown templates:**
357	- `{{var:first_name}}` — recipient's first name
358	- `{{var:training_folder}}` — the **per-cohort mural export** Dropbox folder (from `config.dropboxFolder`). Mark exports the class's murals here after each cohort. This is NOT the workbook.
359	- `{{var:workbook_link}}` — the hosted **course workbook** link, resolved by `deriveWorkbookUrl()` (see "Post-course workbook link" below). Only the templates of migrated courses reference it; when they do, the send is reachability-checked and aborts on a non-200.
360	
361	**Wrapper template:**
362	- `post-wrapper.html` — the MJML-compiled header/footer shell, contains logo, social
363	  links, and footer. The `[EMAIL_BODY]` marker is replaced with rendered Markdown HTML.
364	- Footer variables (`{{ from_name }}`, `{{ from_email }}`, etc.) are replaced at send time.
365	
366	## Key Architecture
367	- `src/cakemail-client.ts` — Cakemail API wrapper (OAuth auth via refresh token, transactional send, contact/list management, campaign create/test/schedule, campaign engagement reports + click logs)
368	- `src/send-course-email.ts` — Sends pre/post-course emails via Cakemail with dedup; enrolls CSM students in follow-up automation
369	- `src/send-newsletter.ts` — Renders a newsletter markdown file into a Cakemail campaign draft; optional test-send and immediate-dispatch flags
370	- `src/send-refresher.ts` — Sends a free-refresher promo to an alumni CSV as direct transactional emails from `SENDER_ID_MARK`, one per recipient; no list, no tagging (see "Refresher offers")
371	- `src/scrape-engagement.ts` — Pulls sent-newsletter engagement from Cakemail (`/reports/campaigns/{id}` for summary metrics, `/logs/campaigns/{id}?filter=type==clickthru` for per-link clicks) and merges into `analytics/email-engagement/newsletter-engagement.json`. Preserves prior pre-Cakemail entries by prefixing Cakemail IDs with `cakemail-` so the two ID spaces never collide. Re-fetches the N most recent campaigns each run (`--refresh-recent`, default 2) to capture late-arriving metrics.
372	- `src/automation-sync.ts` — Shared engine for markdown-driven Cakemail automation templates
373	- `src/render-email.ts` — Markdown-HTML wrapper injection + from/postal/unsubscribe substitution, shared by automation-sync and send-newsletter
374	- `src/refresh-cakemail.ts` — Interactive script to get new refresh token when expired
375	- `src/course-config.ts` — Shared CourseConfig interface, derived fields, calendar URL builders
376	
377	## Cakemail API Gotchas
378	- **Transactional send payload structure** — `POST /v2/emails` requires: `list_id` (integer),
379	  `sender: {id: "..."}` (not email/name), `content: {type: "transactional", subject, html, encoding: "utf-8"}`.
380	  Sender IDs come from `GET /brands/default/senders`. Sender IDs and list IDs are
381	  hardcoded in `cakemail-client.ts`.
382	- **Custom attributes use array format** — `[{"name": "key", "value": "val"}]` not `{"key": "val"}`.
383	  The API returns 422 "value is not a valid list" if you send a dict.
384	- **Email API must be enabled** — returns error 606 "Email API is not enabled" until activated on the account.
385	- **Connection test endpoint** — use `GET /accounts/self`, not `/account`.
386	- **OAuth 2.0 with refresh token** — store refresh token in `.env`, fetch access token
387	  at runtime via `POST /token` with `grant_type=refresh_token`. Access tokens expire
388	  quickly (minutes); refresh tokens may rotate on each use — the client auto-updates
389	  `.env` when this happens. Run `npm run refresh-cakemail` when the refresh token expires.
390	- **Contacts are list-scoped** — custom attributes live on each list, not globally.
391	  API path is `/lists/{list_id}/contacts`. A contact on two lists has independent
392	  attributes on each.
393	- **Tags are list-scoped, and tagging requires list membership — never bypass consent
394	  to apply a tag.** To tag a contact on list X, they must be on list X. That means
395	  any code path that applies a tag to someone who isn't already a member is also
396	  *subscribing* them, and must therefore have explicit consent for that list. Do not,
397	  for example, tag course alumni on the `Newsletter Subscribers` list as a side effect
398	  of sending a post-course email — that quietly enrols them in the newsletter. The
399	  correct pattern is to apply alumni (and similar) tags only after explicit opt-in —
400	  e.g. via the Cakemail form's own tagging on a double-opt-in subscribe, the way the
401	  quiz applies `aiquiz`. When you're about to add tagging logic, ask: "would this
402	  subscribe someone who didn't ask to be subscribed?" If yes, move the tagging to a
403	  place gated by explicit opt-in.
404	- **Transactional email logs have limited lookback** — `GET /v2/logs/emails` defaults
405	  to 7 days. Do not rely on it for dedup; use custom attributes on the Course Students
406	  list instead.
407	- **No official maintained Node.js SDK** — using raw `fetch` against the REST API with
408	  a thin wrapper in `cakemail-client.ts`.
409	- **Variable substitution is local** — templates use `{{var:name}}` placeholders but
410	  substitution happens in Node before sending fully-rendered HTML to Cakemail. No
411	  dependency on Cakemail's template language.
412	
413	## Template Maintenance
414	- Templates in `templates/course/` originated at different times — always
415	  verify placeholder syntax matches what `renderTemplate()` in `send-course-email.ts`
416	  expects before sending. Expected format: `{{var:name}}` for variables,
417	  `{% if var:name %}...{% endif %}` for conditionals.
418	- Variable substitution happens locally in Node before sending raw HTML — Cakemail
419	  receives fully rendered HTML with no template variables.
420	- Delete unused template files rather than leaving them as dead code.
421	
422	## Manual Steps (not yet automated)
423	- Creating lists and subscription forms in Cakemail UI
424	- Authoring the 10-step CSM follow-up automation in Cakemail UI (delays, parent
425	  relationships). Each step picks "Use a template" and imports the matching
426	  `APR CSM Followup NN - ...` template synced by `npm run sync-postcourse-csm`.
427	- Scheduling 2-day emails to specific dates
428

# Course Email Automation

## Location
This CLI lives at `email-automation/` inside the `agile-pain-relief-astro` repo. It has
its own `package.json` and `tsconfig.json`, but shares the **root-level `.env`** with
the Astro site (one source of truth for Cakemail tokens). Env loading
happens via `src/load-env.ts` which points `dotenv` at `../../.env` regardless of the
current working directory. Run commands from inside this directory
(`cd email-automation && npm run ...`). Changes here do not trigger Netlify
rebuilds (see top-level `netlify.toml`).

## Overview
Automates the process of sending pre/post-course emails to students and managing
newsletter distribution. Course emails are sent via Cakemail Transactional Email API.
Post-course CSM follow-up sequences (9 emails) use Cakemail automation triggered by
list addition.

## Commands
```bash
npm run send-course-email -- --course CSM|CSPO|CSD --email pre-7day|pre-2day|post [--csv students/<file>.csv] [--dry-run] [--force]
npm run sync-postcourse-csm [-- --email <01|02|...>] [--dry-run]          # Render the 10 CSM follow-up markdown emails to HTML and upsert them as Cakemail templates.
npm run sync-welcome-newsletter [-- --dry-run]                            # Render the newsletter welcome email and upsert it as a Cakemail template.
npm run sync-ai-welcome [-- --email <01|...>] [--dry-run]                 # Render the AI failure-modes welcome sequence and upsert as Cakemail template(s). Triggered on the `aiquiz` tag (Newsletter Subscribers list).
npm run send-newsletter -- --content newsletters/<file>.md [--test-send <email>] [--send | --schedule <Mon|Tue|Wed|Thu|Fri>] [--allow-past-courses] [--keep-on-error]   # Render a newsletter markdown file and create a draft campaign in Cakemail on the Newsletter Subscribers list. Use --test-send to preview; dispatch with --send (immediate) or --schedule <day> (next that weekday, 10am ET).
npm run refresh-cakemail   # RECOVERY ONLY: mint a fresh refresh token (prompts username + password, grant_type=password) when the current one has fully expired. Prints CAKEMAIL_REFRESH_TOKEN to paste into the root .env. Not needed routinely — the client auto-rotates the token on every run (see Environment).
npm run scrape-engagement [-- --link-details-since <YYYY-MM-DD>] [--refresh-recent <n>] [--output <path>]   # Pull sent-newsletter engagement (opens / clicks / unsubscribes / per-link clicks) from Cakemail and merge into analytics/email-engagement/newsletter-engagement.json.
npm run send-refresher -- --content <promo>.md --audience <list>.csv [--test-send <email>] [--test-name <name>] [--send]   # Direct (transactional) free-refresher promo to an alumni CSV, sent from Mark. No marketing list. See "Refresher offers" below.
npm run ensure-newsletter-attributes   # One-shot: register custom attributes (firstname, lastname, drip_migrated, migrated_at) on the Newsletter Subscribers list.
npm run create-list -- "<list name>"   # One-shot: create a Cakemail list via the API; prints the new list ID to add to shared/cakemail-constants.ts.
```

## Cakemail Course Email Workflow
1. `npm run send-course-email -- --course CSM --email pre-7day --dry-run` — Validate with dry run first
2. `npm run send-course-email -- --course CSM --email pre-7day` — Send for real

The send command reads the Corsizio CSV from `students/`, creates/updates contacts on the
"Course Students" list in Cakemail, sends emails via the transactional API, and sets
custom attributes for dedup — all in one step.

**Late registrant workflow** (student added after initial send):
1. Re-export CSV from Corsizio (includes all students), place in `students/`
2. Re-run the same `send-course-email` command — only the new student gets the email
   (dedup checks Cakemail custom attributes on the Course Students list)
3. Use `--force` to bypass dedup and re-send to everyone

**Post-course workflow:**
```bash
npm run send-course-email -- --course CSM --email post    # Sends immediate post-course email + enrolls in 10-email follow-up
npm run send-course-email -- --course CSPO --email post   # Sends immediate post-course email only (no follow-up sequence for CSPO)
```

All course emails (pre and post) are transactional — sent directly via `POST /v2/emails`.
For CSM post-course, the script also adds the student to the "PostCourse CSM" list,
which triggers the 10-email automation sequence in Cakemail.

## Automation sync (markdown-driven Cakemail templates)

Each automation we maintain lives under `automations/<name>/` as a set of
`NN-slug.md` files with `subject` and `position` in the frontmatter. Currently:

- `automations/csm-followup/` — 10-email CSM post-course sequence.
- `automations/welcome-newsletter/` — single-email newsletter welcome.
- `automations/ai-welcome/` — AI failure-modes welcome/nurture sequence (4-5 emails, email 01 delivers the *AI Failure Modes for Agile Teams* PDF; source-neutral across quiz and direct-download signups). Triggers on the `aiquiz` tag on the Newsletter Subscribers list.

Folder convention: `automations/` holds the live source of truth for every
Cakemail automation we maintain. `exports/` is a historical archive of legacy
campaign JSON, kept for reference — do not add new live content to `exports/`.

### Shared engine

`src/automation-sync.ts` exports `syncAutomation(config)`. It handles
markdown-to-HTML rendering, image-path rewriting, MJML wrapper injection
(via `src/render-email.ts`, shared with the newsletter CLI), merge-tag
substitution, and `upsertTemplate` calls. Each per-automation script (e.g.
`src/sync-postcourse-csm.ts`, `src/sync-welcome-newsletter.ts`) is a thin
wrapper that defines a `AutomationSyncConfig` and calls the engine.

The visible From name and address live in `shared/cakemail-constants.ts`
(`EMAIL_FROM_NAME` / `EMAIL_FROM_EMAIL`), shared by the API client and the
renderer. `src/render-email.ts` owns the inline postal address and unsubscribe
placeholder. Change these and both the automation templates and newsletter
campaigns pick up the new values on next render.

It also inlines brand styles onto `<h1>`–`<h4>` (`styleHeadings`, called from
`renderWrappedHtml`): h2 is dark navy with a brand-blue underline, h3 is brand
blue, both bold. Heading styles are inlined rather than left to the wrapper's
`<head>` `<style>` block because email clients (Gmail especially) strip head
styles, which otherwise leaves headings rendering as plain bold-and-bigger.
Adjust the look in the `HEADING_STYLES` map.

### Adding a new automation

1. Create `automations/<name>/NN-slug.md` files with frontmatter (`subject`, `position`).
2. Put images under `public/images/email/<name>/` in the Astro site.
3. Create `src/sync-<name>.ts`:
   ```ts
   import { resolve } from "path";
   import { syncAutomation } from "./automation-sync";

   syncAutomation({
     name: "<name>",
     emailsDir: resolve(__dirname, "../automations/<name>"),
     wrapperPath: resolve(__dirname, "../templates/course/post-wrapper.html"),
     imageBaseUrl: "https://agilepainrelief.com/images/email/<name>",
     imageSizes: { /* width/height per filename to constrain rendering */ },
     templateName: (email) => `APR <Display Name> ${String(email.position).padStart(2, "0")} - ${email.subject}`,
     testTag: "<name>-test",
     // extraTestMergeTags?: (testEmail) => ({ foo: "bar" }),
   }).catch((err) => { console.error(err); process.exit(1); });
   ```
4. Add an entry to `package.json` scripts: `"sync-<name>": "tsx src/sync-<name>.ts"`.
5. In the Cakemail UI, create the automation; each step picks "Use a template"
   and references the template name produced by `templateName`.

### Idempotency

Re-running a sync updates the existing Cakemail template by name rather than
creating a duplicate — `CakemailClient.upsertTemplate` looks up by exact
template name and PATCHes if found. Rename the template (in config) only if
you intend to orphan the old one.

**Automation step caveat.** Updating a template does **not** propagate to
running Cakemail automations. Each automation step snapshots the template
content at the moment it was configured (empirically confirmed 2026-04-23).
After a content change, re-import the template in each affected automation
step via the Cakemail UI — unselect / reselect "Use a template", or swap to
a different template and back — to force a fresh pull.

### What the engine does per email

- Parses frontmatter (requires `subject` and numeric `position`).
- Renders markdown to HTML via `marked`.
- Rewrites relative `images/foo.ext` paths to the configured `imageBaseUrl`.
- Applies per-filename `imageSizes` to add `width`/`height` attrs and an
  inline style, so email clients don't render at native resolution.
- Injects into the configured MJML wrapper at `[EMAIL_BODY]`, substituting
  `{{from_name}}`, `{{from_email}}`, `{{unsubscribe_link}}`, `{{inline_postal_address}}`.
- Calls `upsertTemplate({ name: templateName(email), subject, html })`.

### Commands

```bash
# CSM follow-up (10 emails)
npm run sync-postcourse-csm -- --email 01 --dry-run     # Render one email and log
npm run sync-postcourse-csm -- --email 01               # Push one email as a template
npm run sync-postcourse-csm                             # Push all 10

# Newsletter welcome (1 email)
npm run sync-welcome-newsletter -- --dry-run            # Render and log
npm run sync-welcome-newsletter                         # Push as a template

# Test-send (works on any automation, sends each selected email
# transactionally to the given address; does not touch templates)
npm run sync-postcourse-csm -- --test-send mark@agilepainrelief.com
npm run sync-welcome-newsletter -- --test-send mark@agilepainrelief.com
```

## Newsletter sender (markdown-driven campaign)

`src/send-newsletter.ts` renders a newsletter markdown file into HTML,
wraps it in the same MJML shell
used by the automation templates, and creates a draft campaign on the
`Newsletter Subscribers` list via the Cakemail `POST /campaigns` API.

**The authoring + send workflow lives in the `/newsletter` skill**
(`.claude/skills/newsletter/SKILL.md`): markdown file format, frontmatter,
Obsidian callouts (`[!quote]` / `[!action]`), the required `courses.json`
block, the `--test-send` / `--send` flag flow, and the sender/compliance notes.
Use that skill to draft or send a newsletter. The command reference below is
retained for quick lookup.

```bash
npm run send-newsletter -- --content newsletters/<file>.md [--test-send <email>] [--send | --schedule <day>] [--allow-past-courses] [--keep-on-error]
```

Every run creates a **brand-new** campaign (`POST /campaigns`); there is no
idempotency. Re-running the command is therefore how the whole list gets
emailed twice. Before creating, the CLI queries `findCampaignsByName` and
**aborts** if a campaign of the same name (`{date} - {subject}`) already exists
in a committed state (scheduled / delivering / delivered). There is **no
`--force`**: delete the existing campaign in Cakemail, then re-run. Same-name
*drafts* don't block (they can't send); they're listed as a cleanup nudge.

Flags:
- `--test-send <email>` creates the draft, then sends a `POST
  /campaigns/{id}/send-test` copy (`type=merged`) to the given address. This is
  the way to preview a newsletter: review it in your inbox and the Cakemail UI.
  **Preview-only: cannot be combined with `--send` or `--schedule`** (dispatch
  in a separate run). Combining preview with dispatch is what previously caused
  a "thought it was just a test" double-send.
- `--send` schedules the draft for immediate delivery (`POST
  /campaigns/{id}/schedule` with no date). Prompts `yes/no` before firing.
- `--schedule <day>` schedules delivery for the next `Mon|Tue|Wed|Thu|Fri` at
  10:00 AM Eastern (`POST /campaigns/{id}/schedule` with a `date` UNIX
  timestamp). Resolves to the soonest future 10am ET on that weekday; the
  `America/New_York` zone keeps it correct across EST/EDT. No confirmation
  prompt (the flag is the intent). Mutually exclusive with `--send`.
- `--allow-past-courses` bypasses the stale-course date check (the CLI aborts
  if `newsletters/courses.json` is missing/empty or holds a past-dated course).
- `--keep-on-error` leaves the draft in Cakemail if test-send or schedule
  fails. Default `DELETE /campaigns/{id}` keeps the UI tidy, since a failed
  send usually means re-running after a content fix.

The campaign is sent from sender ID `SENDER_ID_MARK` (=
`mark@agilepainrelief.com`), not the `contact@` sender used for transactional
course emails. The payload sets `content.default_unsubscribe_link: true`, so
Cakemail appends its own unsubscribe link and mandated postal-address footer.

**Greeting is code-owned, not authored.** `send-newsletter.ts` prepends the
greeting (`GREETING` = `Hi [firstname],`) to the body itself; the markdown file
must not contain one. `[firstname]` is Cakemail's no-fallback merge tag (blank
when the contact has no first name). NEVER use an empty fallback `[firstname,]`
— it's malformed and Cakemail prints the tag literally (this mailed the whole
list a literal `Hi [firstname,],` on 2026-06-26). A no-word fallback is
deliberate (Mark prefers a bare greeting to a generic word like "there"). If an
author still hand-writes a leading line containing `firstname`, `withGreeting()`
strips it and substitutes the canonical greeting, so a mistyped tag can't ship.

## Cakemail Data Model

### Lists
| List | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| **Course Students** | All students. Custom attributes track dedup. Not used for sending. |
| **PostCourse CSM** | Adding a contact triggers 10-email CSM follow-up automation. Per-contact `firstname` and `newslettersignupurl` custom attributes drive template merge tags. |
| **Newsletter Subscribers** | Marketing newsletter campaigns and the `aiquiz` nurture sequence. |

### Tags (broad categories, keep under 15)
- `CSM Student`, `CSPO Student` — course attendance
- Signup tags (`aiquiz`, the two-axis type/source tags) are applied browser-side by the Astro hosted-form POSTs, not by this CLI. See the root `CLAUDE.md` signup sections.

### Refresher offers (free-seat promos to alumni)

When a workshop has spare seats, we offer a free refresher to past students who opted in. The audience is built from tags, not a standing list. **Audience rule (apply all three filters):**

1. **Include** anyone tagged `Interested - Refresher - {COURSE}` (e.g. `Interested - Refresher - CSM`).
2. **Exclude** anyone tagged `DO NOT NOTIFY - Refresher - {COURSE}` — a hard suppression. If a contact carries *both* the Interested and DO-NOT-NOTIFY tags, DO-NOT-NOTIFY wins.
3. **Exclude anyone who has already attended a refresher.** A refresher attendee carries a `Course - <date> - …` tag for the refresher *session* date, distinct from their original paid training. Cross-reference against the known refresher session dates below and drop matches. Don't offer the same person a second free refresher.

**Known past refresher session dates** (extend this when you run a new one):
- `2026-03-05` — CSM refresher (Mar 5–6, 2026)
- `2025-07-14`, `2025-07-15` — CSPO refresher (Jul 14–15, 2025)

**Maintenance note:** the date-list approach works but is brittle. The cleaner durable signal is a dedicated `Attended - Refresher - {COURSE}` tag applied to attendees of each free refresher — then filter 3 becomes a single tag check with no date table to maintain. Prefer adding that tag going forward, and reduce the date list as attendees get the tag.

**Delivery:** use the dedicated `npm run send-refresher -- --content <promo>.md --audience <list>.csv` script (`src/send-refresher.ts`). It sends as a **direct (transactional) send** via `sendTransactional()` (`/v2/emails`), one rendered email per recipient, and does **not** create a standing Cakemail list. The transactional endpoint's `list_id` is only relay context (`Course Students`); it does not subscribe recipients as marketing contacts, so there's no list to maintain and no consent side effect. The script already sends from `SENDER_ID_MARK` (not the `SENDER_ID_CONTACT`/contact@ used by default transactional sends, since refresher promos go from Mark) and applies **no tags** — attendance tags (`Attended - Refresher - {COURSE}`) are added after the workshop, not when the offer goes out. Preview with `--test-send <email>` (sends one copy and stops); dispatch to the whole audience with `--send`. Unsubscribe is handled automatically: Cakemail appends an unsubscribe button to the transactional email's footer (confirmed by inspecting a test send), so no manual compliance footer is needed; the template's reply-to-opt-out p.s. is a friendly extra, not the sole mechanism.

Source-of-truth audience today lives in the migration exports (`migration/all-people.csv`, `migration/subscribers-people.csv`); the filtered CSM list is materialized to `migration/refresher-csm-interested.csv`.

### Custom Attributes (on "Course Students" list)
Pattern: `{type}_course_date`, `{type}_7day_prep_sent`, `{type}_2day_prep_sent`, `{type}_post_sent`

Example for CSM: `csm_course_date`, `csm_7day_prep_sent`, `csm_2day_prep_sent`, `csm_post_sent`

The `send-course-email` script sets these after successful sends and checks `*_sent`
attributes for dedup on subsequent runs.

### Custom Attributes (on "PostCourse CSM" list)
Set at enrollment time by `send-course-email --email post --course CSM`:
- `firstname` — the student's first name from the Corsizio CSV. Referenced in templates
  as `[firstname,there]`, so students without a value see "Hello there!".
- `newslettersignupurl` — per-student prefilled Cakemail form link (to the Astro
  site's `/newsletter-subscribe/` page) that subscribes them to the Newsletter
  Subscribers list. Built by `buildPrefillSignupUrl()` in `src/signup-url.ts`.
  Referenced in templates as `[newslettersignupurl]`.

Re-running `send-course-email` for a student who already exists on this list PATCHes
the existing contact's attributes rather than re-inserting (so re-enrollment refreshes
the signed URL).

### Newsletter Opt-In (prefilled form link)
Post-course emails include a "Subscribe to the Newsletter" link pointing at the Astro
site's `/newsletter-subscribe/` page, with the student's email and first name prefilled
in the query string (and `auto_submit=1`). That page embeds a Cakemail form on the
Newsletter Subscribers list with double opt-in; Cakemail's form-prefill script fills and
submits it from the URL params, then sends the confirmation email.

The placeholder `CAKEMAIL_NEWSLETTER_SIGNUP_URL` in post-course markdown templates is
replaced per-student inside `renderMarkdownEmail()` using `buildPrefillSignupUrl()` from
`src/signup-url.ts`. No HMAC signature, no server endpoint, no OAuth token — double
opt-in is the abuse guard (a forged link only mails a confirmation to the address that
owns it).

## Environment
All env vars live in the **root-level `.env`** (one directory above this one), shared
with the Astro site. The CLI loads it via `src/load-env.ts` on import. Required keys:

- `CAKEMAIL_REFRESH_TOKEN` — OAuth refresh token for this CLI. **Routine refresh is
  automatic:** every run exchanges it for a short-lived access token, and if Cakemail
  issues a rotated refresh token in that response, `cakemail-client.ts` writes the new
  value back to the root `.env` itself (no manual step). Only when the refresh token has
  fully **expired** (the client throws `Cakemail refresh token expired. Run: npm run
  refresh-cakemail`) do you run `npm run refresh-cakemail` to mint a new one from
  username + password and paste it into the root `.env`.
- `NEWSLETTER_SIGNUP_BASE_URL` — optional, defaults to `https://agilepainrelief.com`.
  Base URL for the per-student post-course newsletter subscribe link (the
  `/newsletter-subscribe/` page); override for local testing.

List IDs and sender IDs live in `../shared/cakemail-constants.ts`, imported by
`src/cakemail-client.ts`.

## Course Config
Create `courses/<type>-<location>.json` (e.g. `csm-virtual.json`, `cspo-virtual.json`, `csd-virtual.json`) with fields:
type, date, numberOfDays, muralLink, meetingInvite (object)

`--course CSM` auto-detects the config by matching files in `courses/` whose name starts with the course type (case-insensitive); it errors if zero or multiple match.

`meetingInvite` is a structured object, both fields copied off the same Zoom screen:
- `zoomUrl` — full Zoom one-click join URL (e.g. `https://us02web.zoom.us/j/...?pwd=...`). Drives the "JOIN the COURSE ZOOM MEETING" button. The `pwd=` token is Zoom's one-click join token.
- `invitationUrl` — Zoom's `/meetings/{id}/invitations?signature=...` link. The email links to it for "all other ways of joining" (phone dial-in numbers, dial-in passcode, SIP). We do **not** scrape or restate those details: Zoom maintains that page, so it stays current automatically when a dial-in number changes. The `signature` token is scoped to the meeting and lives for its lifetime.

The former `passcode` field (plus a hardcoded dial-in number list) is gone. `send-course-email` rejects any config that still has `meetingInvite.passcode`, so an un-migrated config breaks loudly instead of sending a broken invite.

Optional fields (have defaults):
- `duration` — daily start-end time, e.g. `"08:59-17:01"` (default). Drives both the calendar links and the displayed `{{var:class_times}}` in the pre-course emails (e.g. CSD uses `"12:30-17:00"` → "12:30 p.m. to 5:00 p.m.").
- `timezone` — IANA timezone, e.g. `"America/Toronto"` (default)
- `location` — e.g. `"Virtual"` (default), `"In-Person"`
- `googleDocsFolder` — only needed for CSM courses
- `dropboxFolder` — the **per-cohort mural export** Dropbox folder (post-course only). Shown in the post email as `{{var:training_folder}}`. This is where Mark exports the class's murals after the cohort; it is per-cohort and unrelated to the workbook.
- `workbookUrl` — optional per-cohort override for the hosted workbook link. Normally omitted (the link is resolved by course type; see below). Set it only for a one-off cohort that needs a different URL.

### Post-course workbook link

Two different links live in the post-course email, and they are deliberately separate:

- **Mural export** — `{{var:training_folder}}`, from the per-cohort `config.dropboxFolder`. Changes every cohort. Still on Dropbox (out of scope for the workbook move).
- **Course workbook** — `{{var:workbook_link}}`, the workbook PDF hosted on the APR site. Resolved by `deriveWorkbookUrl(config)` in `src/course-config.ts`: (1) `config.workbookUrl` cohort override, else (2) `courses/workbook-urls.json[type]`, else `null` (course not yet migrated — its template then still hardcodes its own link).

`courses/workbook-urls.json` maps course type → the current direct PDF URL on the APR site (`https://agilepainrelief.com/materials/<course>-<year>-q<quarter>-<hex>/<file>.pdf`). It is the **single place to update once per quarter** when the site's `/materials/` slug rotates. Must be the direct PDF URL (bare files have no folder index) with spaces `%20`-encoded.

`{{var:workbook_link}}` appears in all three CSPO templates — `pre-7day` and `pre-2day` (the "Download the Digital Workbook" link, the pre-class firewall-critical one) and `post` — so migrating a course means switching each of its templates to the variable. (CSM/CSD still hardcode their Dropbox links pending migration.)

When any email's template (pre or post) references `{{var:workbook_link}}`, that send (including `--dry-run`) requires a configured URL and runs `assertWorkbookReachable()`: a `HEAD` (falling back to a ranged `GET`) that **aborts on a non-200**, so a typo'd slug, an unpushed folder, or a filename mismatch can't email students a dead link. The check is scoped to `agilepainrelief.com/materials/` URLs. It proves the link is *live*, not that it's the *current* workbook. Templates that still hardcode a Dropbox link are unaffected until migrated.

Derived automatically:
- `dateFormatted` (e.g. "Feb 17-18"), `daysOfWeek` (e.g. "Tuesday-Wednesday") — from `date` + `numberOfDays`
- `zoomLink` — from `meetingInvite.zoomUrl`
- The `{{var:meeting_invite}}` block — a short "Other ways to join" line linking to `meetingInvite.invitationUrl`

Google Calendar and Outlook Calendar links are generated from config fields by `src/course-config.ts`.

### Pre-course Email Template Placeholders
The pre-course HTML templates (`templates/course/pre-*.html`) use `{{var:name}}` variables
that are substituted locally in Node before sending raw HTML to Cakemail:
- `{{var:first_name}}`, `{{var:course_dates}}`, `{{var:class_times}}`, `{{var:meeting_invite}}`
- `{{var:google_calendar_url}}`, `{{var:outlook_calendar_url}}`
- `{{var:mural_link}}`, `{{var:zoom_link}}`, `{{var:google_docs_folder}}`
- `{{var:workbook_link}}` — the hosted course workbook PDF (see "Post-course workbook link"; despite the heading, the same variable is used by the pre-7day / pre-2day templates for the "Download the Digital Workbook" link)

### Post-course Markdown Email Templates
Post-course emails are written in Markdown (`templates/course/post-csm.md`, `post-cspo.md`)
with YAML frontmatter for the subject line. At send time, Markdown is converted to HTML
via `marked` and injected into `templates/course/post-wrapper.html` (the MJML-compiled
header/footer shell).

**Available variables in Markdown templates:**
- `{{var:first_name}}` — recipient's first name
- `{{var:training_folder}}` — the **per-cohort mural export** Dropbox folder (from `config.dropboxFolder`). Mark exports the class's murals here after each cohort. This is NOT the workbook.
- `{{var:workbook_link}}` — the hosted **course workbook** link, resolved by `deriveWorkbookUrl()` (see "Post-course workbook link" below). Only the templates of migrated courses reference it; when they do, the send is reachability-checked and aborts on a non-200.

**Wrapper template:**
- `post-wrapper.html` — the MJML-compiled header/footer shell, contains logo, social
  links, and footer. The `[EMAIL_BODY]` marker is replaced with rendered Markdown HTML.
- Footer variables (`{{ from_name }}`, `{{ from_email }}`, etc.) are replaced at send time.

## Key Architecture
- `src/cakemail-client.ts` — Cakemail API wrapper (OAuth auth via refresh token, transactional send, contact/list management, campaign create/test/schedule, campaign engagement reports + click logs)
- `src/send-course-email.ts` — Sends pre/post-course emails via Cakemail with dedup; enrolls CSM students in follow-up automation
- `src/send-newsletter.ts` — Renders a newsletter markdown file into a Cakemail campaign draft; optional test-send and immediate-dispatch flags
- `src/send-refresher.ts` — Sends a free-refresher promo to an alumni CSV as direct transactional emails from `SENDER_ID_MARK`, one per recipient; no list, no tagging (see "Refresher offers")
- `src/scrape-engagement.ts` — Pulls sent-newsletter engagement from Cakemail (`/reports/campaigns/{id}` for summary metrics, `/logs/campaigns/{id}?filter=type==clickthru` for per-link clicks) and merges into `analytics/email-engagement/newsletter-engagement.json`. Preserves prior pre-Cakemail entries by prefixing Cakemail IDs with `cakemail-` so the two ID spaces never collide. Re-fetches the N most recent campaigns each run (`--refresh-recent`, default 2) to capture late-arriving metrics.
- `src/automation-sync.ts` — Shared engine for markdown-driven Cakemail automation templates
- `src/render-email.ts` — Markdown-HTML wrapper injection + from/postal/unsubscribe substitution, shared by automation-sync and send-newsletter
- `src/refresh-cakemail.ts` — Interactive script to get new refresh token when expired
- `src/course-config.ts` — Shared CourseConfig interface, derived fields, calendar URL builders

## Cakemail API Gotchas
- **Transactional send payload structure** — `POST /v2/emails` requires: `list_id` (integer),
  `sender: {id: "..."}` (not email/name), `content: {type: "transactional", subject, html, encoding: "utf-8"}`.
  Sender IDs come from `GET /brands/default/senders`. Sender IDs and list IDs are
  hardcoded in `cakemail-client.ts`.
- **Custom attributes use array format** — `[{"name": "key", "value": "val"}]` not `{"key": "val"}`.
  The API returns 422 "value is not a valid list" if you send a dict.
- **Email API must be enabled** — returns error 606 "Email API is not enabled" until activated on the account.
- **Connection test endpoint** — use `GET /accounts/self`, not `/account`.
- **OAuth 2.0 with refresh token** — store refresh token in `.env`, fetch access token
  at runtime via `POST /token` with `grant_type=refresh_token`. Access tokens expire
  quickly (minutes); refresh tokens may rotate on each use — the client auto-updates
  `.env` when this happens. Run `npm run refresh-cakemail` when the refresh token expires.
- **Contacts are list-scoped** — custom attributes live on each list, not globally.
  API path is `/lists/{list_id}/contacts`. A contact on two lists has independent
  attributes on each.
- **Tags are list-scoped, and tagging requires list membership — never bypass consent
  to apply a tag.** To tag a contact on list X, they must be on list X. That means
  any code path that applies a tag to someone who isn't already a member is also
  *subscribing* them, and must therefore have explicit consent for that list. Do not,
  for example, tag course alumni on the `Newsletter Subscribers` list as a side effect
  of sending a post-course email — that quietly enrols them in the newsletter. The
  correct pattern is to apply alumni (and similar) tags only after explicit opt-in —
  e.g. via the Cakemail form's own tagging on a double-opt-in subscribe, the way the
  quiz applies `aiquiz`. When you're about to add tagging logic, ask: "would this
  subscribe someone who didn't ask to be subscribed?" If yes, move the tagging to a
  place gated by explicit opt-in.
- **Transactional email logs have limited lookback** — `GET /v2/logs/emails` defaults
  to 7 days. Do not rely on it for dedup; use custom attributes on the Course Students
  list instead.
- **No official maintained Node.js SDK** — using raw `fetch` against the REST API with
  a thin wrapper in `cakemail-client.ts`.
- **Variable substitution is local** — templates use `{{var:name}}` placeholders but
  substitution happens in Node before sending fully-rendered HTML to Cakemail. No
  dependency on Cakemail's template language.

## Template Maintenance
- Templates in `templates/course/` originated at different times — always
  verify placeholder syntax matches what `renderTemplate()` in `send-course-email.ts`
  expects before sending. Expected format: `{{var:name}}` for variables,
  `{% if var:name %}...{% endif %}` for conditionals.
- Variable substitution happens locally in Node before sending raw HTML — Cakemail
  receives fully rendered HTML with no template variables.
- Delete unused template files rather than leaving them as dead code.

## Manual Steps (not yet automated)
- Creating lists and subscription forms in Cakemail UI
- Authoring the 10-step CSM follow-up automation in Cakemail UI (delays, parent
  relationships). Each step picks "Use a template" and imports the matching
  `APR CSM Followup NN - ...` template synced by `npm run sync-postcourse-csm`.
- Scheduling 2-day emails to specific dates

# Unguessable slug for course workbooks

## Context

Course workbooks (read-only class / post-class reference PDFs) moved off Dropbox because some clients' corporate firewalls block Dropbox but treat `agilepainrelief.com` as a normal business site. The materials are low-sensitivity, and delivery is by emailed link to attendees.

## Decision

Serve workbooks as static PDFs under `public/materials/<course>-<year>-q<quarter>-<16 hex>/`, guarded only by an unguessable path plus an `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow` header (`netlify.toml`, scoped to `/materials/*`). No login or auth gate. The folder rotates per course each quarter; old folders are left in place. See the "Course workbooks" section of `CLAUDE.md` for the mechanism and runbook.

## Considered options

- **Real auth gate** (Netlify password protection / Cloudflare Access / an edge-function token) — rejected as disproportionate for low-sensitivity reference material, and it adds friction for attendees. This is the path to revisit if content sensitivity ever rises.
- **Keep it on Dropbox / Google Drive / email attachments** — rejected: the firewall block is the whole reason for the move, and attachments are unreliable at size.

## Consequences

- The entropy lives entirely in the `openssl rand -hex 8` suffix; the readable prefix is guessable on purpose. The `noindex` header is the *sole* search-engine guard, because a PDF has no HTML `<meta>` fallback.
- `/materials/` is deliberately **not** listed in `robots.txt`. A `Disallow` would stop compliant crawlers from *fetching* the file, so they would never see the `noindex` header (the two are in tension). This looks like an oversight but is intentional.
- The unguessable slug defends against guessing/enumeration, not leakage. Link unfurling, `Referer` headers, and human forwarding can still expose a URL. Quarterly rotation guards *future* materials from an *old* leaked link; it does not revoke past access.

# Project History

A short, human-readable log of notable changes and the reasoning behind them.
Newest first. (Detailed, current behaviour lives in `CLAUDE.md`; this file is the
"why we did it" story.)

## 2026-07-27 — The quiz gets its designed look: semantic colour, balance bar, cover strip

**Why.** The quiz shipped functionally correct and visually generic, because the
design existed only as in-chat mockups that were never saved to a file. The
handoff carried a five-line prose summary of them, so the build reproduced the
prose and none of the design. Mark then wrote the mockups up properly (section
11 of the implementation handoff: colour roles with reference hexes, type rules,
component-by-component layout, icon mapping), which is what this entry builds.

**What we did.**
- **A visual system, not styling.** Colour now encodes one of four meanings
  (valuable / slipping / context / recommendation) and is always backed by an
  icon, a label and a position, so it survives greyscale and colour-blindness.
  Slipping is amber, never red: red reads as failure, and this quiz refuses to
  grade anyone. Surfaces went flat (hairline borders, no shadows, no gradients),
  type went serif-over-sans at two weights, and the palette lives as
  `--color-quiz-*` tokens in `global.css` so a restyle is a token edit, not a
  component edit. The accent is APR brand blue, as the spec directs.
- **Result page rebuilt** around a **balance bar**: one flat bar showing the
  proportion of gaining to slipping answers, with no number, letter or tier
  title on it. That replaced the old band headline entirely. Below it, two
  iconned cards, a visibly softer context strip for the constraints, and the one
  move as an accent callout with the only heavy border on the page, because it
  is the payoff. The labels Mark had parked as "cringe" are settled by the

`package.json` `overrides` pins `@astrojs/markdown-remark` to `7.2.0`. Added 2026-06-14 after `npm run update` bumped astro 6.3.7 → 6.4.4 and broke the build with: `feed.xml ... does not provide an export named 'unified'`.

**Root cause:** astro 6.4.4 imports `{ unified }` from `@astrojs/markdown-remark` (added in 7.2.0) and exact-pins 7.2.0. But `@astrojs/mdx@5.0.6` exact-pins the older 7.1.2 (no `unified`). Two exact pins → two copies that can't dedupe; the 7.1.2 copy won the hoisted top-level slot, so the bundled feed route resolved its bare import to 7.1.2 and crashed. 7.2.0 is a minor superset of 7.1.2 (only added exports), so forcing it everywhere is safe for mdx 5.0.6.

**How to apply / remove:** The proper long-term fix is bumping `@astrojs/mdx` 5 → 6 (6.0.3+ depends on 7.2.0 natively). The repo's `^5.0.3` range can't reach mdx 6, and mdx 6.0.3 was <7 days old so `min-release-age=7` blocked it. Once `@astrojs/mdx` is on ^6 (and its markdown-remark dep is ≥7.2.0), **drop this override** and verify `npm run build` renders `/feed.xml` + `/glossary/feed.xml`.

# Project Memory

## MDX Formatting Rules
- **Imports must use straight quotes** — never curly quotes in import statements (e.g., `import X from '@/path'` not `import X from '@/path'`)
- **Use actual Unicode characters, not escape sequences** — write `'` `"` `"` `–` directly, never `\u2019`, `\u201c`, `\u201d`, `\u2013`
- **YAML frontmatter** — use HTML entities for special characters (e.g., `"` for quotes, `'` for apostrophes, `–` for en-dash) since raw curly quotes can cause YAML parsing issues
- See [formatting-patterns.md](formatting-patterns.md) for detailed glossary entry structure
- [Glossary external links go in the reference section](feedback-glossary-external-links-in-references.md) — name the source in body prose, put the `https://` link in the Resource Links / Related Books box; inline only internal links

## Marketing Experiments
- [Experiment result conventions](feedback-experiment-results.md) — "Not run" is not "Failed"; classify by whether the experiment actually executed

## Working style
- ["What action would we take?" litmus test](feedback-action-litmus.md) — default to dropping tags/data unless a concrete campaign or segment will use them; Mark runs the business alone and any kept data imposes maintenance cost
- [Never commit/push/PR on Mark's behalf](feedback-no-git-checkin.md) — stop at "diff is ready"; Mark handles all check-in steps himself
- [No URLs inline in social-media post text](feedback-no-urls-in-post-text.md) — URL belongs only in the dedicated `url` field; the posting pipeline handles placement
- [AI Failure Modes quiz: frame as knowledge test](feedback-ai-failure-quiz-framing.md) — "test your knowledge of how AI fails", not "twelve questions on how AI fails"; challenge framing converts better than learning-resource framing
- [LinkedIn AI-skeptical posts need a caveat](feedback-linkedin-ai-caveat.md) — short, varied one-liner reframing failure-mode critique as prerequisite to using AI well, not rejection. LinkedIn only; skip on non-AI posts.
- [No redirects for noIndex or short-lived pages](feedback-no-redirects-ephemeral-pages.md) — nothing to preserve; just delete them
- [No confirmation prompts in CLI scripts](feedback-no-confirmation-prompts.md) — gate actions behind an explicit flag + default-safe dry run, not a type-"yes" prompt; running the command is the intent

## API design
- [No booleans in caller-facing APIs](feedback-no-booleans-in-apis.md) — prefer string enums (`'none' | 'within-sections'`) over `true/false`; booleans are unreadable at the call site

## External service quirks
- [Cakemail lowercases all tags](reference-cakemail-lowercase-tags.md) — writing CamelCase is fine (readability), but reads / comparisons / UI-segment queries must use the lowercased form
- [Cakemail contact lookup filter syntax](reference-cakemail-contact-filter.md) — `?email=` is silently ignored; use `?filter=email==<value>` or dedup/idempotency breaks invisibly
- [Cakemail form submission replaces tags](reference-cakemail-form-replaces-tags.md) — hosted-form POST overwrites the whole tag set (not merge); risk of wiping `aiquiz`. Tags auto-create, applied even to existing contacts
- [Bluesky counts URLs as 15 chars](reference-bluesky-url-char-count.md) — toward the 300-char limit, URLs cost 15 chars (not full length). LinkedIn and Mastodon still count full length.
- [Cakemail token auto-rotates](reference-cakemail-token-auto-rotate.md) — refresh token rotates automatically every run (client writes new value to root .env); `refresh-cakemail` is recovery-only for full expiry, no `--purpose` flag
- [Cakemail merge-tag empty fallback breaks](reference-cakemail-merge-tag-empty-fallback.md) — `[firstname,]` renders literally; use `[firstname]` (no comma) for no fallback.
